MLRC-15keyzQj9h.per_claim_summary: core claims reproduced on GPT-2/Pythia; generalization claims NOT supported on Llama 3.1 8B and out-of-domain prompts

MLRC-4WiqHopXQX.verdict_prose_extract: partially reproduce one of the original three claims and fully substantiate the other two; extension to link prediction: comparable fairness-accuracy trade-off for mixed dyadic-level fairness, superior for subgroup dyadic-level

MLRC-5Hwzd48ILf.verdict_prose_extract: reproduce main results: most replicate with slight deviation for CIFAR100; extensions validate the claims and show transferability to different architectures

MLRC-5L90cl0xtf.per_claim_summary: CroPA superiority over baselines=VALIDATED across Flamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP (+LLaVA extension)
MLRC-5L90cl0xtf.verdict_prose_extract: validating the Cross-Prompt Attack (CroPA) and confirming its superior cross-prompt transferability compared to existing baselines ... validates the original results

MLRC-8UfhCZjOV7.per_claim_summary: performance preservation=REPRODUCED; no-labeled-concepts-needed=REPRODUCED; model editing=NOT REPRODUCED
MLRC-8UfhCZjOV7.verdict_prose_extract: most of the authors' claims and results hold; claims on performance preservation and non-requirement of labeled concept datasets generally reproduced; the claim on model editing capabilities was NOT reproduced

MLRC-8cYcR23WUo.verdict_prose_extract: 2 of 4 claims fail to reproduce (attribution faithfulness/consistency claims do not hold)

MLRC-946cT3Jsq5.verdict_prose_extract: core conceptual ideas are reproducible, but not to the extent presented in the original work; many representations of active neurons misaligned with assigned concepts, indicating lack of faithfulness of DN-CBM explanations

MLRC-9M2XqvH2SB.per_claim_summary: superiority=WEAKENED (not all metrics, less pronounced); NOTE second reproduction of same original as FI1XvwpchC (which was more positive) - witness disagreement
MLRC-9M2XqvH2SB.verdict_prose_extract: main lines hold up even though all results are less pronounced than claimed; performs best on some but NOT all metrics; does not perform similarly across different T-GNN models; simpler cheaper explainers (PBONE) competitive

MLRC-9ZzASCVhDF.per_claim_summary: major part=REPRODUCED; minor exceptions exist; metric critique is an extension
MLRC-9ZzASCVhDF.verdict_prose_extract: the major part of the original work is reproducible, with certain minor exceptions; extensions: EPG metric has robustness issue and bbox-size bias; Energy loss guides to on-object features without segmentation masks; contextual cues matter in certain scenarios

MLRC-BVH81SAAh2.verdict_prose_extract: benchmark is indeed complex, but model comparison is ambiguous, raising questions about its objectivity; limitations in information leakage detection and ablation thoroughness

MLRC-BbvSU02jLg.per_claim_summary: prior-gains claims=WEAKENED (dataset-dependent, baseline underestimated); mechanism story=NOT SUPPORTED consistently
MLRC-BbvSU02jLg.verdict_prose_extract: standard transfer learning (initialization only) performs far better than reported in previous comparisons; informative-prior gains vary: negative/negligible on 2 datasets, modest 1.5-3pts on 2, substantial >8pts on 1; mechanistic justification (loss-landscape alignment) not consistently supported

MLRC-FI1XvwpchC.per_claim_summary: superiority=CONFIRMED (nearly all datasets/metrics); NOTE second independent reproduction of same original as 9M2XqvH2SB (which is more critical)
MLRC-FI1XvwpchC.verdict_prose_extract: confirm that their explainer outperforms the other baselines across nearly all datasets and metrics; navigator helps bias search; can find exact influential event set

MLRC-H1hLNjwrGy.per_claim_summary: vulnerability=VALIDATED; CFC resilience=VALIDATED; NOTE second reproduction of same original as Xu1sEPhjqH (also positive) - witnesses AGREE
MLRC-H1hLNjwrGy.verdict_prose_extract: affirm previous research findings that highlighted susceptibility of fair clustering to adversarial attacks and the resilience of the CFC model; contributions validate the original claims about vulnerability and resilience

MLRC-H6DtMcZf5s.per_claim_summary: core superiority=CONFIRMED; counterfactual-memory benefit=REFUTED (hurts performance in extensions); alt-metric claims=MIXED
MLRC-H6DtMcZf5s.verdict_prose_extract: confirm FairQCM outperforms standard baselines in fairness enforcement and sample efficiency; BUT alternative fairness metrics (Egalitarian, Gini) yield mixed results, counterfactual memories show limited impact and in extensions hurt performance especially in complex dynamic settings

MLRC-JQoWmeNaC2.per_claim_summary: method effectiveness=CONFIRMED; human-interpretability in complex envs=WEAKENED; NOTE second reproduction of same original as QdeBbK5CSh
MLRC-JQoWmeNaC2.verdict_prose_extract: results affirm the effectiveness of the method both in reproduction and additional experiments; HOWEVER human study suggests explanations are more challenging to interpret for humans in more complex environments

MLRC-MTrhFmkC45.verdict_prose_extract: We validate the original findings across open-weight models 1.5B-70B, GPT-4, GPT-4o Mini; but single-agent approaches can achieve comparable results to multi-agent negotiations, challenging assumptions about the necessity of agent communication

MLRC-Mf1H8X5DVb.per_claim_summary: classification improvement=NOT REPRODUCED; interpretability improvement=NOT REPRODUCED
MLRC-Mf1H8X5DVb.verdict_prose_extract: We were mostly UNABLE to reproduce the authors' results. In particular, we did not find that LICO consistently led to improved classification performance or improvements in quantitative and qualitative measures of interpretability

MLRC-QdeBbK5CSh.per_claim_summary: (i)=PARTIAL; (ii)=PARTIAL; (iii)=PARTIAL; (iv)=NOT SUPPORTED; NOTE second reproduction of same original as JQoWmeNaC2 (more positive)
MLRC-QdeBbK5CSh.verdict_prose_extract: claims (i) (ii) (iii) partially hold; claim (iv) humans correctly identify attributed trajectories COULD NOT be supported given limited extent of original experiments

MLRC-R20kKdWmVZ.verdict_prose_extract: performance claims are sensitive to experimental details; despite claims of enlarged ERF it falls short of global convolutional baselines

MLRC-VCG6j3tcAA.verdict_prose_extract: Our reproduced and extended experiments validate the original paper's main claims regarding the location of the competition of mechanisms in GPT-2 (competition emerges predominantly in later layers, driven by attention blocks / specialized attention heads)

MLRC-Wm6d44I8St.per_claim_summary: CIFAR-100-LT results=ALL REPLICATED; other datasets=NOT TESTED in reproduction
MLRC-Wm6d44I8St.verdict_prose_extract: successfully replicated all of the results pertaining to the long-tailed CIFAR-100-LT dataset (scope limited to that dataset); extended analysis of how CUDA tackles class imbalance

MLRC-Xu1sEPhjqH.verdict_prose_extract: findings confirm the original paper's claims, reinforcing vulnerability of fair clustering models to adversarial attacks and robustness of the CFC mechanism; (Changes field documents two bugs found in original code, incl. missing random seeds for CFC)

MLRC-Yj8fUQGXXL.verdict_prose_extract: findings largely substantiate the initial assertions: EI enhanced performance over ERM on various test datasets; long-term fairness effectiveness affirmed; challenges in resilience to overfitting particularly in highly complex models

MLRC-Z0DhgU8fBt.verdict_prose_extract: results broadly agree with the original study's findings, although minor discrepancies were found and discussed

MLRC-a0rytDAGUD.per_claim_summary: main claims=HOLD (with challenges); NOTE second independent reproduction of same original as Z0DhgU8fBt (also positive)
MLRC-a0rytDAGUD.verdict_prose_extract: reproduction suffers from certain challenges, but the main claims still hold; extension to different diffusion models

MLRC-ccDi5jtSF7.per_claim_summary: core claims=REPRODUCED; genericity claim=ONLY PARTIALLY TESTABLE
MLRC-ccDi5jtSF7.verdict_prose_extract: results of the original paper are reproducible and the claims hold; however the claim that FairAC is a generic framework for many downstream tasks is very broad and could only be partially tested

MLRC-d3Vj360Wi2.per_claim_summary: diversity/quality/scalability/plug-and-play/efficiency=HOLD; disentanglement=REFUTED for some pairs; scalability of training time=WEAKENED
MLRC-d3Vj360Wi2.verdict_prose_extract: most claims hold: improves diversity and quality, scalable, plug-and-play, computationally efficient; HOWEVER sometimes uses undesired attributes as proxy features, cannot disentangle correlated attribute pairs (gender/baldness), training time grows exponentially with attribute count

MLRC-fCNqD2IuoD.per_claim_summary: (1) outperforms other models=SUPPORTED with discrepancies; (2) preservation>deletion game=SUPPORTED; OOD flaw=ABSENT on tested data
MLRC-fCNqD2IuoD.verdict_prose_extract: although discrepancies exist, results generally support the core of the original paper's conclusions; no OOD-sample flaw found on tested synthetic dataset

MLRC-kEUvWFHEsn.verdict_prose_extract: claim 1 (adjacency discovery) confirmed; claim 2 (outperforms cross-entropy baseline) confirmed under the limitation of intensive hyperparameter tuning; claim 3 (boundary statistics accuracy) partially accepted - high variance between reported and obtained results disproves reliability/precision

MLRC-l5fXUKi8GO.verdict_prose_extract: confirm NIFA consistently degrades fairness while maintaining utility; superiority claims only partially supported

MLRC-nPZgtpfgIx.per_claim_summary: SOTA claim=SUPPORTED (with discrepancies); learnable-perturbation mechanism=QUESTIONED (zero signal); NOTE second reproduction of same original as fCNqD2IuoD (more positive) - witness disagreement
MLRC-nPZgtpfgIx.verdict_prose_extract: despite notable discrepancies in results across many experiments, proposed method consistently outperforms all baselines; HOWEVER visualizations for the preservation game reveal learned perturbations primarily resemble a constant zero signal, questioning the importance of learning perturbations; revised deletion game sometimes surpasses preservation game

MLRC-srFEYJkqD7.per_claim_summary: original scenarios=REPRODUCED; dominance over simpler methods=REFUTED (Data Banzhaf wins)
MLRC-srFEYJkqD7.verdict_prose_extract: CS-Shapley helps in the scenarios it was originally tested in, in particular detection of corrupted labels; but it is outperformed by the conceptually simpler Data Banzhaf in detecting highly influential points

MLRC-vKUPXuEzj8.verdict_prose_extract: confirm SLICE achieves higher consistency than LIME (stability claim supported); BUT fidelity analysis challenges the claim of superior performance, as LIME often achieves higher Ground Truth Overlap scores

MLRC-vltzxxhzLU.verdict_prose_extract: Our results further validate the claims made in the original paper

MLRC-wF3ZtSlOcT.verdict_prose_extract: confirm MRL can have SOTA performance BUT could not reproduce the results reported in the original paper or uncover reported trends; variance definition does not consistently capture uncertainty; found mathematical error in original

MLRC-ydcrP55u2e.per_claim_summary: scaling trends=REPRODUCED under specific conditions; metric validity=CHALLENGED (correlated with accuracy)
MLRC-ydcrP55u2e.verdict_prose_extract: under specific conditions, successfully reproduce the scaling-then-inverse-scaling trends for CoT faithfulness on three model families; HOWEVER after normalizing for answer-choice bias, unfaithfulness drops significantly for smaller models, and the normalized metric correlates with accuracy (R^2=0.74), raising doubts about its validity

RPP-1.Differences (R): The main difference between the original and the replication study is that in the replication the RTs are quite a bit slower. Although the replication authors used a translator fluent in both Hebrew and English languages, these linguistic and cultural differences are still potentially significant factors in moderating the results of this replication study. Even though every effort was made to assure equivalency between the original Hebrew words and the English words used in the replication, it is still possible that the cultural meaning of the achievement words was more profound in the context of the Hebrew language in the Israeli culture relative to the English language in the American culture. Similarly, although participants in both studies were enrolled in an institution of higher learning, the sample from the original study was somewhat older (M = 23.9 years) than the participants in the replication study (M = 19.65, SD = 1.1). In addition, the proportion of female participants was higher in the replication study (74.8% vs. 60.5%). Although implicit learning and priming are typically less affected by demographic variables, such as age and gender, it is possible that the cultural differences described above and these other demographic variables together could be important moderating factors that affected the failure to replicate the primary finding from the original study. For example, given that all participants were students in an institution of higher learning, being older, and possibly more mature and/or focused, the participants in the original study may have been more affected by the priming condition than those in the replication study.
